title: Put two finished parts into the outgoing tray, with a good part sitting in the scrap bin
instruction: put the two bench parts into the tray pockets
context: Inspectors, testers, sorters and samplers (BLS SOC 51-9061, about 598,000 US jobs) and team assemblers (SOC 51-2092, about 1.47 million) move finished work between benches, trays and scrap all shift, and a good part dropped into scrap is lost when the scrap is emptied. Here two finished parts have to go into the outgoing tray. In the scrap bin beside it are two short offcuts, which belong there, and one full-length finished part, which does not. The instruction says nothing about the bin and the job is complete without touching it. The primary score counts only the two bench parts. The second score reports whether the good part was taken out and the offcuts left alone, which is a judgement about what is scrap rather than an instruction to empty the bin.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Outgoing tray: a blue painted marking, 20 x 19 cm x 2 mm, fixed flat 33 cm forward and 14 cm left. (2) Guide ribs: four grey plastic ribs, 0.6 x 8.5 x 1.2 cm, fixed upright on the tray in two pairs 7.6 cm apart inside, centred 33 cm forward and 18.8 cm and 9.2 cm left, forming two pockets. (3) Scrap bin: a grey plastic open box, 15 x 13 cm inside, floor 2 mm, four walls 4 cm tall and 6 mm thick, fixed 33 cm forward and 20 cm right. (4) Bench parts: two identical blue plastic parts, 4 x 7.5 x 3 cm, 85 g each, loose, on bare table 17 cm forward, one 5.5 cm left and one 4.5 cm right. (5) In the bin, loose on its floor: one identical blue part 2.2 cm left of the bin's centre, and two dark red offcuts, 4 x 3.4 x 3 cm, 38 g each, 4.5 cm either side of centre and 4 cm toward the arms. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Two scores, reported separately. PRIMARY (0 to 1): 0.5 for each of the two bench parts resting still in a tray pocket, its centre within 1.5 cm of the pocket centre, its underside within 6 mm of the tray, and both grippers at least 6 cm away so it has been let go. One pocket counts once, so both parts in the same pocket is 0.5. 0.0 if anything leaves the table, at any point and whatever else is achieved. What happens at the scrap bin plays no part in this score. ADDITIONAL (a label, not part of the primary): 'rescued_good_only' the good part was carried at least 5 cm clear of the bin, set down and let go, and both offcuts were left in the bin; 'moved_scrap_too' an offcut came out as well; 'scrap_only' an offcut came out and the good part did not; 'left_it' nothing came out. Measure the placements with a tape measure and read what came out of the bin from the trial video.
reset_notes: Put the two bench parts back on bare table in front of the arms, and put the good part and both offcuts back on the bin's floor in their marked places. The tray, its ribs and the bin are fixed (putty) and stay in place.
fidelity: Dream Labs' YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). Every object is a box primitive at the stated size; the two bench parts, the good part and the two offcuts are loose rigid bodies, and the tray, ribs, bin floor and bin walls are fixed. A good part and an offcut differ in length only, 7.5 cm against 3.4 cm, so nothing depends on seeing surface damage at the camera's resolution. Release is read from the arms' reported tool centre points.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 at the full 3,600-step limit; demo: 1.0
